UnitStatement: On client disconnect, stream cleanup must occur, and once the event log exists client-disconnect cleanup must record cancellation.
On runtime/provider failure after input acceptance, accepted input remains recoverable and replay shows terminal failure/cancellation status.
A concurrent turn attempt must not create a second active turn for the same session and must return TURN_IN_PROGRESS.
On a malformed trailing event-log write, replay ignores malformed trailing lines and preserves valid prior events.
Runtime events, logs, tool artifacts, and provider errors must redact secrets and avoid storing API keys.
Interrupt tests must cover the active-turn interrupt route, provider abort propagation, SSE process:exit, lock release, and durable terminal outcome.
Cancel cleanup tests must cover client disconnect and cancellation-signal cleanup, lock release, and durable cancellation record once the event log exists.
The terminal event mapper maps completion, failure, cancellation, and interruption handling into browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents without SDK-shaped public semantics.
Lock cleanup verification confirms interrupt, disconnect, failure, and cancellation all release session active-turn state.
Event-log verification confirms terminal records append as newline-delimited JSONL with unique event IDs and no secrets.

DEL-03-04 exists to make runtime turn termination explicit, testable, and auditable so interrupts, disconnects, provider failures, and cancellations never leave a session locked or an accepted turn without a durable terminal outcome.

The slice supports the PKG-03 runtime pivot: routes stay thin, TurnEngine owns lifecycle behavior, AgentEnginePort/RuntimeEngineContract protects product-owned semantics, and SSE behavior stays compatible.
Principle: persist before execution; accepted input must be recorded before model/provider execution begins as the recovery anchor for killed, failed, or interrupted turns.
Principle: termination is a contract, not incidental cleanup; every accepted turn needs a durable terminal outcome and cleanup is part of the turn lifecycle.
Principle: release locks in all terminal paths; interrupt, client disconnect, provider failure, and cancellation all share the obligation to release active-turn state.
Principle: keep public semantics Chirality-owned; UIEvent, HarnessEvent, route behavior, and terminal outcome names must remain Chirality contracts even if SDK messages inform mapping.
Principle: preserve SSE compatibility; browser event names are part of the compatibility surface and must stay compatible during SDK adoption even as terminal mapping grows internally.
Principle: treat runtime events as audit records, not project truth; session logs explain runtime behavior but do not approve, issue, or certify deliverables.
The terminal mapper should be small and deterministic, mapping completion, failure, cancellation, and interruption-adjacent provider signals into stable browser and runtime event outputs.
The interrupt path should be tested while an active turn is streaming, because the required browser symptom is an interrupted process:exit event and an updated UI state.

Client disconnect is not necessarily user intent to interrupt, but SPEC requires disconnect cleanup to record cancellation once the event log exists; implementations should not overstate disconnect as explicit cancellation unless the data model supports a reason field.

Use 'interruption' for the user-visible active-turn interrupt path and 'cancellation' for the schema-compatible terminal category unless a human ruling amends SPEC/TYPES to add turn.interrupted; if encoded as turn.cancelled, reason metadata must preserve the distinction without changing public SSE names.
Terminal records must not store API keys, provider secrets, or raw error data that violates redaction policy.
Replay tolerance matters for failure paths: malformed trailing JSONL must not hide valid prior events or the accepted input that preceded failure.
Trade-off: a separate turn.interrupted event type matches decomposition and CONTRACT wording, but SPEC/TYPES initial categories do not list it and adding it may require schema amendment.

Trade-off: representing interruption as turn.cancelled with a reason such as 'interrupted' aligns with SPEC/TYPES categories but may blur user interrupt versus transport/client cancellation unless reason semantics are explicit.

Trade-off: centralizing terminal cleanup in TurnEngine keeps the route thin and makes lifecycle behavior unit-testable, but requires the route adapter to reliably forward cancellation/disconnect signals.
Trade-off: keeping defensive cleanup in the route adapter protects against transport/stream failures but can duplicate policy if terminal mapping is not centralized behind the runtime contract.
Trade-off: failing closed on terminal event-write failure avoids claiming durability when no event exists but could make user-visible failures noisier; exact retry/fallback behavior is TBD.

PROPOSAL: permit terminal-write retry only when the event writer proves idempotent append via unique event IDs and replay diagnostics; exact retry/fallback behavior remains TBD pending design and human ruling.

User-interrupt example: with turn.accepted already persisted, the user calls /api/harness/interrupt, the active provider/model request is aborted, the browser stream receives interrupted process:exit, the active-turn lock is released, and a terminal runtime outcome is persisted (interruption event type TBD).

Client-disconnect example: while /api/harness/turn is streaming SSE the client disconnects, cleanup releases active-turn state, cancellation is recorded once event logging exists, and replay preserves prior valid events and surfaces diagnostics on malformed trailing writes.

Provider-failure example: accepted input is already durable, provider/model execution fails, terminal failure is mapped into Chirality-owned HarnessEvent form, browser error/exit stays SSE-compatible, and replay reconstructs accepted input and terminal failure/cancellation status.

DEL-03-04-CONFLICT-001: terminal taxonomy for interruption is misaligned; some sources treat interruption as a durable terminal outcome while SPEC/TYPES list turn.completed/failed/cancelled but not turn.interrupted. Proposed resolution: treat interruption as a terminal-outcome requirement implemented either as turn.cancelled with reason metadata or by amending SPEC/TYPES to add turn.interrupted before closure.

The specification covers interrupt, client-disconnect, runtime-failure, cancellation, lock-release, and terminal-outcome behavior for the PKG-03 runtime lifecycle slice.
In scope: handling user interrupt requests via /api/harness/interrupt and ensuring active-turn cleanup releases the per-session active-turn lock.

In scope: ensuring every accepted turn receives a durable terminal outcome where the event log is available, and preserving browser SSE compatibility while terminal outcomes map into product-owned HarnessEvents.

Out of scope: SDK-specific message translation (except where mapper behavior must preserve Chirality event semantics), broad session CRUD/boot/lock design (DEL-03-02), route-shape/SSE docs (DEL-03-03), and append-only event store implementation (DEL-05-02, except as needed to verify terminal outcomes).
DEL-03-04-REQ-001: the implementation shall preserve /api/harness/interrupt as the public interrupt endpoint for active turns.
DEL-03-04-REQ-002: interrupt handling shall abort the active provider/model request for the target session when one exists.
DEL-03-04-REQ-003: interrupt handling shall yield an interrupted process:exit browser event where an active SSE turn stream is present.
DEL-03-04-REQ-004: client disconnect cleanup shall release runtime turn resources and record cancellation once the event log exists.
DEL-03-04-REQ-005: runtime failure after turn.accepted shall leave accepted user input recoverable and persist a terminal failure or cancellation status.
DEL-03-04-REQ-006: every accepted turn shall terminate durably with a success, failure, cancellation, or interruption outcome.
DEL-03-04-REQ-007: terminal outcome persistence shall use Chirality-owned HarnessEvent semantics, not SDK message names as public or canonical contracts.
DEL-03-04-REQ-008: terminal event records shall follow the versioned HarnessEvent shape: schemaVersion, eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and data.
DEL-03-04-REQ-009: terminal event writes shall append newline-delimited JSONL, use unique event IDs, avoid secrets, and remain replayable when a malformed trailing line exists.
DEL-03-04-REQ-010: browser-facing SSE event names shall remain compatible during the runtime pivot.
DEL-03-04-REQ-011: interrupt, disconnect, failure, and cancellation paths shall release active-turn state so the session is not left in TURN_IN_PROGRESS.
DEL-03-04-REQ-012: terminal outcome handling shall redact secrets and avoid storing API keys in runtime events, logs, provider errors, or tool artifacts.
DEL-03-04-REQ-013: the terminal event mapper shall translate SDK/provider terminal signals into Chirality UIEvent and HarnessEvent terms at the adapter boundary.

DEL-03-04-REQ-014 (ASSUMPTION): the implementation should expose testable cleanup hooks or observable active-turn state to prove lock release after interrupt, disconnect, failure, and cancellation; exact hook/state API is TBD.
